argument: Both candidates satisfy D1-D5 and D7-D14. They separate on D6. Across the seven populated constructor families R1's p90 spans 0.0323-0.1394 (ratio 4.3) and its p99 spans 0.38-1.84 (ratio 4.9); R2's p90 spans 0.0293-1.0285 (ratio 35.1) and its p99 spans 0.90-12.14 (ratio 13.4). R2 systematically inflates rate-bearing families (C1, C6, C7) because dividing by calibration RMS penalises coordinates whose calibration mean sits near zero - a property of the constructor, not of range support. R1 divides by the calibration RANGE, which is the natural scale of the empirical support itself, and is therefore constructor-neutral by construction. R1 also has the cleaner one-sentence reading.
